profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Denver - Englewood) is located at 8636 S Peoria Street, Englewood, CO 80112. The operator publishes a footprint of 240549 square feet and 18 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18. This building sits in the Denver-Aurora corridor local reporting has dubbed "Data Center Row," which also includes a major QTS facility under construction in Aurora. Xcel Energy, the region's dominant utility, said in 2025 it was seeking to invest $22 billion to add 12 to 14 gigawatts of new generation and transmission capacity by 2040, driven substantially by data center demand; the utility reported pending data center applications for 5.8 gigawatts of electricity, nearly matching its entire existing 6.2-gigawatt Colorado generating capacity, with data center load projected to reach 8.5 gigawatts by 2040, per Colorado Sun's reporting. The Colorado Public Utilities Commission has voiced skepticism about the reliability of these forecasts, noting that between October and May alone, seven data center prospects representing 4 gigawatts withdrew requests while more than a dozen new prospects totaling 3.5 gigawatts filed applications, with regulators and consumer advocates warning that ratepayers could face stranded-asset costs if projected demand fails to materialize.

The QTS facility anchoring the Aurora side of "Data Center Row" is planned at 177 megawatts of capacity on 80 acres at the I-70/C-470 interchange, positioned to become Xcel Energy's largest industrial customer in Colorado, on par with Evraz Rocky Mountain Steel in Pueblo, a marked shift from Xcel's historical major customers in mining and manufacturing, per Colorado Sun's 2023 reporting. That single campus is expected to require 160 megawatts of peak load delivered via a $28 million high-voltage transmission line, ramping up over roughly a decade, with Xcel anticipating similar-scale loads from other emerging data center customers in the region. For QTS, electricity was reported to represent about 40% of operating costs, underscoring why competitive utility rates were central to the Aurora site decision, a dynamic shared broadly across Colorado's Front Range data center corridor.

reading.body:
Flexential Denver - Englewood publishes 18 MW of IT capacity across 240,549 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 18 MW supports roughly 450 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation average, the same power supports roughly 1,800 racks. The operator has not published a rack count, a power density target, or a cooling architecture, so which end of that range applies here is not determinable from the spec page.

The seven certifications cover distinct requirements. SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II qualify the facility for regulated financial and operational workloads. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense and aerospace data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security controls. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard under which the SOC reports are issued, not a separate operational credential. Together these certifications make the campus eligible to host a wide range of compliance-sensitive workloads, but which tenants are actually present is not published.

Among the 17 Colorado facilities this site has mapped, Englewood is ranked first by published IT capacity, and it accounts for all 18 MW of the published total for the state. That ranking is an artifact of disclosure, not necessarily of physical scale: only one of the 17 mapped facilities publishes a megawatt figure, so 16 sites contribute nothing to the comparison. Colorado sits within reach of large Rocky Mountain renewable generation, but grid interconnection details and power sources for this campus are not published in the operator's specifications.
